name: David Kaplan
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026); SEC insider holdings (2025)
forbes_bio: David Kaplan is a cofounder of credit-focused alternative investment firm Ares Management, which manages $596 billion in assets.
Kaplan has been at Ares since 2003 and previously spent three years at venture firm Shelter Capital Partners and a decade at Apollo Global Management.
He currently serves as a director and partner of Ares and was previously co-chairman of its private equity business.

name: Fuat Tosyali
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2020); Forbes annual (2018-2019); Hurun Global (2020-2022)
forbes_bio: Fuat Tosyali is CEO of steel and iron producer Tosyali Holding, which has 18 facilities spread over Turkey, Serbia and Algeria.
At age five, he began working with his father in a small workshop in Iskenderun, where they made sheet metal out of used tin cheese cans.
From sheet metal, they went on to bucket and stove production. The family began investing in Algeria in 2008.
Including overseas operations, Tosyali is on track to become Turkey's largest iron and steel producer, with an 8.5 million ton capacity by 2019.
Fuat shares ownership in the business with younger brothers Ayhan and Fatih Tosyali, who are also billionaires.
forbes_facts: By the end of 2019, Tosyali Holding expects to have invested in excess of $6 billion in integrated production facilities located in Oran, Algeria.
Fuat Tosyali flies on his private jet to visit operations in Algeria every week.

name: Ginia Rinehart
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Ginia Rinehart is the youngest child of Australian mining mogul Gina Rinehart.
Together with her three siblings, she is the beneficiary of a trust that owns a substantial stake in mining giant Hancock Prospecting.
She stayed out of a bitter court battle to wrest control of the trust from her mother.
She has a degree in business, majoring in Spanish, from London.
Hancock disclosed that as of September 2023 it had provided A$5.44 billion for dividends that will be paid after the dispute between Bianca and her brother John against their mother is resolved.
forbes_facts: She once worked as a publicist at the House of Faberge in London.
She was previously engaged to the son of the Beach Boys' Bruce Johnston.

name: Pavel Demidov
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Pavel Demidov is the founder of Dominant Group, one of Russia's largest sugar producers, which  boasts more than 790,000 acres of agricultural land in the country.
The group also owns four dairy plants and is among Russia's top ten cheese makers.
In the 1990s Demidov worked as deputy CEO of Alfa-Eco, a company founded by fellow billionaire Mikhail Fridman, which has interests in the sugar trade.
Demidov has a 50% stake in Dominant, his wife, Svetlana, owns the remaining 50%.
forbes_facts: Dominant Group processes 50,000 tons of sugar beet per day through its seven sugar plants.

name: Yigal Dimri
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025)
forbes_bio: Yigal Dimri is the CEO and owner of the real estate group Y.H. Dimri, a Tel Aviv-based real estate business.
Y.H. Dimri is one of the largest residential construction companies in Israel, operating in the residential, office, and commercial real estate sectors.
He began his career as a renovation contractor in 1980 together with his father and established Y.H. Dimri in 1989.
In 2004, the company went public, and its securities are traded on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange.

name: Brad Kelley
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2006-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Brad Kelley, a Kentucky native and a farmer's son, built a fortune from discount cigarettes.
He built Commonwealth Brands, maker of USA Gold and Malibu cigarettes, and sold it for $1 billion in 2001.
Kelley has since used that cash to become one of the largest landowners in the U.S., with over 500,000 acres from Hawaii to Florida.
Kelley owns historic stud farm Calumet in Kentucky, which had three starters in the 2017 Kentucky Derby.
forbes_facts: In 2020, Kelley sold travel guide Lonely Planet, which he had bought seven years earlier from the BBC for $75 million.
His horse English Channel has sired offspring that have nabbed over $57 million in prize money.

name: Chung Yong-ji
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026)
forbes_bio: Chung Yong-ji is the founder and CEO of South Korean biotechnology company Caregen, best known for its anti-wrinkle treatment and diabetes supplement.
U.S.-educated Chung founded Caregen in 2001 and listed on Korea's technology-rich Kosdaq stock exchange in 2015.
Caregen sells its products to more than 130 countries, and its biggest markets are in the Middle East and North Africa, Europe and Asia Pacific regions.
The company's other major revenue source is an injectable product called Dr. CYJ Hair Filler, which claims to help regrow hair.

name: Andrei Molchanov
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Andrey Molchanov and his family owns a controlling stake in LSR Group, the biggest producer of construction materials (sand, brick, broken stone) in Russia.
LSR is also one of the leading real estate developers, with a portfolio of 8.3 million square meters of space.
Molchanov is a native of St. Petersburg, where his stepfather worked as vice governor for 10 years.
Molchanov's son Egor is a member of the board at LSR Group.

name: Itamar Locks
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2024); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Itamar Locks is the son-in-law of Lucia Maggi, who cofounded Andre Maggi Group with her late husband, Andre Maggi.
Amaggi is one of Brazil's largest producers of soybeans and other commodities.
Lucia Maggi cofounded the business with her husband in 1977 and took over as majority shareholder after he died in 2001.
After Andre Maggi died in 2001, his son Blairo Maggi took over as the chief executive of the company.
Locks is one of the controlling shareholders of Amaggi, along with Blairo Maggi, and Hugo de C. Ribeiro.
forbes_facts: Locks previously served as the president of the agricultural division of Amaggi.
Amaggi produces approximately 1.2 million tons of soy, corn, and cotton in Brazil each year.

name: Ramesh Chandra Sharma
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2022); Hurun India (2017-2019)
forbes_bio: Ramesh Chandra Sharma gets his wealth from a majority stake in non-banking finance company Capri Global Capital, which is run by his son Rajesh Sharma.
Mumbai-based Capri offers home loans, construction loans  as well as customized business loans for medium and small-scale enterprises.
It has more than 100 branches across India, with a substantial presence in northern and western India.
forbes_facts: Capri Global started as a construction finance company in 2011.
Capri Global forayed into housing finance in 2017.
